args.title: checkout-api: rollback to v2.3.0 after v2.3.1 failed production health checks
args.summary:
checkout-api v2.3.1 (deployed to all production regions: us-east, us-west, eu-west) failed health checks, with error rate elevated to ~18% and service reporting unhealthy in all regions.

Remediation: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent version with a healthy production record (v2.2.9 healthy, v2.3.0 healthy, v2.3.1 unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc was a staging-only release).

The first rollback attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error, halting after us-east — leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout across all three regions.

Current state: All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down to ~0.2%.

Follow-up: Root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is not yet known; v2.3.1 should not be re-deployed until investigated. Also worth reviewing the orchestrator error that caused the partial rollback.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did get created despite the timeout (INC-0001, open). Done.

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api v2.3.1 was live in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and unhealthy, with error rate at ~18%. Deployment history showed v2.2.9 healthy → v2.3.0 healthy → v2.3.1 unhealthy (v2.3.1-rc was staging-only, so not a candidate). **v2.3.0 was the most recent release healthy in production.**

**Rollback:** The first attempt to roll back to v2.3.0 failed partway with an orchestrator error, halting after us-east — which left the fleet in a *mixed* state (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on the broken v2.3.1). I re-verified state, retried, and the retry completed cleanly.

**Verified final state:** all three regions on v2.3.0, service `healthy: true`, error rate down to ~0.2%.

**Incident:** INC-0001, SEV2, open — documents the failure, the rollback, the partial-failure/retry, and the current healthy state.

Two things worth flagging for follow-up (noted in the incident):
- Root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is still unknown — v2.3.1 shouldn't be redeployed until it's investigated.
- The orchestrator error that caused the partial rollback is a reliability gap worth investigating; had I not re-checked status after the error, the fleet would have been left half-rolled-back with two regions still serving bad traffic.

Should I do them in parallel? The incident description depends on rollback result. So sequential.

Retry the rollback — it might be idempotent-ish and continue for remaining regions.

transcript.content: The retry succeeded. Verifying health across all regions.
transcript.reasoning_content: Now verify health, then open SEV2 incident.
